sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-2: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function
OpenStax Biology 2e, 28.1 Phylum Porifera (oxygen by diffusion)

note.text: This is a close-up of a membrane with water on both sides.

steps.title: Membrane
steps.instruction: Trace the membrane down the middle, with its gaps.

note.text: Some small molecules can pass through a cell membrane on their own.

steps.title: Molecules
steps.instruction: Dab a dot for every molecule.

note.text: There are many molecules on the left: a high concentration. Few on the right: a low concentration.

steps.title: Net movement
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from left to right.

note.text: Molecules move randomly all the time, but more cross from the crowded side to the emptier side. This is diffusion.
This is the same place a while later.
Diffusion needs no energy from the cell. It's a kind of passive transport.

steps.title: Spread out
steps.instruction: Dab a dot for every molecule.

note.text: Now the concentration is equal on both sides. Molecules still move, but there's no net movement: equilibrium.

steps.title: Which way?
steps.question: Which way do the molecules diffuse overall?

options.text: From the crowded left side to the emptier right side
options.feedback: Yes. Diffusion goes from high concentration to low until it evens out.
That's from low to high. Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.
Molecules are always moving. Overall, more cross from the crowded side.

options.text: Only when the cell pushes them
options.feedback: Diffusion needs no push from the cell. It happens on its own.

steps.title: Speed
steps.question: How would warming the water change diffusion?

options.text: It would speed up, because molecules move faster when warmer
options.feedback: Right. Higher temperature gives molecules more energy, so they spread out faster.
Warmer molecules move faster, so diffusion speeds up.
Warmth speeds molecules up. Diffusion goes faster.
Temperature matters: warmer molecules move faster, so diffusion speeds up.

steps.title: In living things
steps.question: A sponge's cells use up oxygen. How does more oxygen get into them from the seawater?

options.text: It diffuses in, from the water where there's more oxygen to the cells where there's less
options.feedback: Yes. Sponges get oxygen by diffusion, and carbon dioxide diffuses out the same way.

options.text: The cells make their own oxygen
options.feedback: Sponge cells use oxygen; they don't make it. It diffuses in from the water.

options.text: Oxygen moves from low to high
options.feedback: Diffusion goes from high to low: from the water into the cells.
Their mitochondria need oxygen, which diffuses in from the water.
